steps.title: Sign up
steps.body: Use Google or an email link. You'll also confirm you're 18 or older before checkout — that's required to run a paid bot.

steps.title: Meet Emcee
steps.body: One bot, Emcee. It already does emotes, greets guests, keeps the room in check, and has an outfit — more skills are on the way.

steps.title: Connect your bot
steps.body: Paste your bot's access code and your room's ID. We show you exactly where to find both, and how to give the bot permission to work in your room.

steps.title: Go live
steps.body: The bot joins your room and the dashboard shows it's live. Change any setting and it updates in seconds — no restart needed.

comparison.title: Everyone else made the room owner do the work.

rows.alt: Renting a bot for in-game Gold
rows.weakness: Against Highrise's rules, no dashboard, no one to call if it breaks — you're trusting a stranger.
rows.answer: Pay with a card, manage everything yourself, and see exactly how your bot is doing at all times.

rows.alt: Building your own with a coding template
rows.weakness: You'd need to know how to code, settings are buried in files, and nobody's watching if it goes offline.
rows.answer: Two-minute setup, plain forms instead of code — we take care of keeping it running.

rows.weakness: An unwatched room. It feels quieter and less fun when you're not around.
rows.answer: Cheap enough that trying it is an easy yes.

items.title: Your bot, your account
items.body: You create the Highrise bot account and its access code — we just host and run it for you. We never own or control your bot's account.

items.title: Never any Highrise Gold
items.body: Every price on this page is real money (cards). We never accept, hold, or move Highrise Gold — that's against the rules and we won't touch it.

items.title: Built the right way
items.body: Our bots run on Highrise's own official bot technology, made by the game's creators. You just fill in settings — there's no coding involved.

pricing.title: One price. One bot. One room.
pricing.subtitle: Each bot instance connects to one room. Pay by card — your bot is live as soon as checkout completes.

botShowcase.title: Meet Emcee. It grows with you.
botShowcase.subtitle: One bot, one subscription, one setup — it doesn't get swapped out as new skills are added. Your room's full-time host: it entertains, greets guests, keeps things in order, and looks the part.

emote.name: Emotes
emote.body: Type an emote's name in chat and your avatar performs it — even ones you don't own. The room owner can call one out for everyone to do at once.

concierge.name: Greeter
concierge.body: Privately welcomes every guest, remembers regulars each time they come back, and gives VIPs on your list an extra-special welcome.

warden.name: Moderation
warden.body: Filters bad language, blocks spam, and hands out warnings with a clear paper trail — watching your room around the clock, all set up with simple toggles.

avatar.name: Avatar
avatar.body: Dress your bot in an outfit you choose, give it a spot to stand, and a little idle animation — so it feels present instead of just floating there.

music.name: Music
music.body: Still an early idea, not yet planned out — more details soon.

config.heading: Configuration

general.title: Bot language
general.description: Language the bot uses for its own built-in responses — emote confirmations, loop messages, moderation warnings, mod-command replies. Doesn't change your own custom templates (Welcome, VIP, Farewell, Activation message) — those stay exactly as you wrote them.

emoteOnSay.title: Emote on say
emoteOnSay.description: Someone types an emote's name (or its number from the "emotes" list) in chat — no command needed — and their avatar performs it, even if they don't own it. Loops on repeat by default (see Loop below).
emoteOnSay.disabledEmotesDescription: These won't trigger just by saying their name in chat. "all <emote>" and "loop <emote>" can still use them directly — this only blocks the passive say-it trigger.

emoteAll.title: Emote all
emoteAll.description: "all <emote>" makes everyone in the room perform it as a staggered wave.
emoteAll.permissionDescription: Who's allowed to start an all-room wave: just you, you plus anyone with Designer rights in this room, or a specific list of usernames.

listCommand.title: Emote list command
listCommand.description: "emotes" whispers a paginated list of available emote names.

loop.title: Loop
loop.description: On by default: saying an emote's name (or "loop <emote>" explicitly) repeats that emote until the user says "stop" or leaves the room — the AFK-dance feature. Turn off to make emotes fire once instead, like before.
loop.enabledDescription: On by default — every emote-on-say trigger loops, not just "loop <emote>". This is the most demanding feature we offer; keep an eye on things in busy rooms, and turn it off to go back to a single emote per trigger.
loop.maxDurationDescription: Safety auto-stop in case someone forgets to say "stop" — for example if they close the app instead of properly leaving the room.
loop.cooldownDescription: Minimum wait between one user starting new loops.

activationMessage.title: Activation message
activationMessage.description: Posted publicly in room chat the moment the bot connects — not a whisper. Off by default.
activationMessage.enabledDescription: Off by default — an unprompted public message on every reconnect can get noisy.
activationMessage.templatePlaceholder: e.g. I'm online and ready to help in {room_name}!
activationMessage.cooldownDescription: Skip the announcement if the bot already posted one within this many minutes — guards against a reconnect storm spamming the room.

welcome.title: Welcome messages
welcome.description: Whispered to a guest when they join — skipped entirely for VIPs, who get their own greeting instead.
welcome.templatesDescription: Use {username}, {room_name}. Rotates through the list on each greeting so the room doesn't feel repetitive.
welcome.cooldownDescription: Don't whisper the same person again until this many hours have passed since their last greeting.
welcome.busyModeEnabledDescription: Skip greetings entirely while joins are coming in faster than the threshold below, so a raid or event doesn't flood whispers.
welcome.quietHoursEnabledDescription: Skip greetings during a daily window (e.g. overnight).

vip.title: VIP recognition
vip.description: Named regulars get a distinct greeting instead of the generic welcome — always, even during busy mode or quiet hours.
vip.announceToRoomDescription: Also post a public chat line when a VIP joins, not just the whisper.
vip.emoteCelebrationEnabledLabel: Play an emote on VIP join

farewell.title: Farewell
farewell.description: Logs when a regular (visits ≥ the threshold below) leaves. No whisper is possible — they're already gone — but an optional public send-off can post instead.
farewell.minVisitsLabel: Minimum visits to count as a regular
farewell.publicMessageDescription: Off by default — a public message on every qualifying leave gets noisy fast.

anchorSpot.title: Anchor spot
anchorSpot.description: Two ways to set where the bot stands: say "anchor" in-game, or enter coordinates directly on this page. Either one updates the same saved spot — the bot walks back there every time it reconnects instead of appearing wherever the room drops it.
anchorSpot.enabledDescription: Turns off both ways of setting the spot — the in-game "anchor" command and the coordinate fields below.

position.withPosition: Nudge the saved spot's coordinates directly — an alternative to standing in the room and saying "anchor". Always just you.
position.withoutPosition: No spot saved yet. Say "anchor" in-game once to set a starting point, or enter coordinates directly if you already know them. Always just you.
position.roomLayoutDescription: Highrise rooms only come in a fixed set of floor plans — pick the one this room uses so the preview lines up with the real floor. You can change it anytime.
position.gridHint: Click a tile to set X/Z.

idleEmote.title: Idle emote loop
idleEmote.description: The bot performs a low-key emote on a repeat interval whenever it isn't busy responding to something — a little life instead of standing frozen.
idleEmote.enabledDescription: Off by default — a sustained background action, same caution as the Emotes skill's loop feature.
idleEmote.emoteDescription: Emote from the Emotes skill's list.

reactionBack.title: Reaction back
reactionBack.description: Someone reacts at the bot — the bot reacts back the same way.
reactionBack.cooldownDescription: Minimum wait between reacting back at the same person, so repeated reactions can't be used to spam the bot's actions.

defaultOutfit.title: Default outfit
defaultOutfit.description: A fixed outfit the bot wears when it connects. Items must be owned by the bot (or free) — anything it doesn't own is skipped rather than blocking the whole outfit.
defaultOutfit.itemIdsDescription: Search and add items the bot owns.

outfitPresets.title: Named outfit presets
outfitPresets.description: "look <name>" switches the bot into a saved outfit.
outfitPresets.presetsDescription: Give each preset a name, then search and add the items it should wear.

outfitClone.title: Copy a look
outfitClone.description: "copy <username>" makes the bot wear as much of that person's current outfit as it actually owns — items it doesn't own are skipped, never bought.
outfitClone.minMatchDescription: If fewer than this many of the target's items are actually in the bot's own inventory, skip the copy entirely and say why, instead of applying a near-empty outfit.

filter.title: Word filter
filter.description: Custom terms trigger a private, whisper-only warning to whoever said them — never a public callout — and count toward the warnings below.
filter.customTermsDescription: Matching ignores capitalization and common tricks like repeated letters, so simple attempts to sneak past it won't work.

antiSpam.title: Anti-spam
antiSpam.description: Catches message flooding and copy-pasted repeats. A trip counts toward the warnings below, same as a filter hit.
antiSpam.messageRateCountDescription: More than this many messages from one person within the window below trips the anti-spam rule.
antiSpam.duplicateCountDescription: Sending the exact same message this many times in a row trips the rule.

strikeEscalation.title: Warning escalation
strikeEscalation.description: A filter hit, anti-spam trip, or !warn command adds a warning. Crossing a threshold below takes the matching action — only the highest one reached fires, not every one below it.
strikeEscalation.strikeDecayDescription: A user's warning count resets after this many hours with no new warnings.
strikeEscalation.banEnabledDescription: Off by default — the most serious action we offer, kept opt-in.
strikeEscalation.banAtStrikesDescription: Always requires at least 2 warnings, regardless of this setting.

exemptions.title: Exemptions
exemptions.description: Exempt users skip the filter and anti-spam entirely, and can issue moderation commands in chat. The room owner is always exempt.

modCommands.title: Moderation commands
modCommands.description: In-chat commands for exempt users: warn, mute, and kick a named user. Ban is dashboard-only, not available as a chat command.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
intro: BotMaker (“we,” “us”) runs a subscription service that hosts configurable Highrise bots on your behalf. This page explains what personal data we collect through the dashboard and your bot instances, why we collect it, and the choices you have.

We built this product for a Highrise audience that skews young, so we’ve tried to write this in plain language rather than dense legal boilerplate. If anything here is unclear, email us — see “Contact” below.

whoWeAre.heading: Who we are
body: BotMaker is an independent, unofficial project, operated by CodeSwift (codeswift.com.br). We are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Highrise or Pocket Worlds — “Highrise” is referenced only to describe what our bots connect to.

We’re a Brazil-based company. We’ll publish our registered legal name, CNPJ, and business address on this page once they’re finalized; until then, you can reach us at the contact address below, or at codeswift.com.br.

whatWeCollect.heading: What we collect
body: Account info: your email address, and if you sign in with Google, the name and profile photo Google shares with us.
Age attestation: a timestamp confirming you told us you’re 18 or older — we don’t collect your birthdate or an ID.
Billing details: handled by Stripe. We never see or store your full card number; we keep your Stripe customer ID, subscription status, and invoice history.
Your bot’s access token: encrypted the instant it reaches our servers. It’s write-only — we display only the last 4 characters, and no one, including us, can read it back out in full.
Room activity your bot generates: chat and event data needed for the features you turn on (for example, moderation logs or greeting history), linked to Highrise user IDs, not to our own accounts.
Product usage: which pages and features you use, so we can tell what’s working. Session recording is off, and we never capture what you type into the token field.
Your language preference, so emails and the dashboard show up in the right locale.

whyWeCollect.heading: Why we collect it
body: To run the service: connect your bot, apply your configuration, and show you its status.
To bill you and prevent fraud, through Stripe.
To email you things you actually need to know: sign-in links, a payment problem, or your bot going down.
To enforce our Terms and keep the platform we run on healthy — including suspending instances used for harassment or spam.
To meet our own tax, accounting, and legal obligations.

howLongWeKeep.heading: How long we keep it
body: Room event logs are kept for 90 days, then reduced to anonymized daily counts — the detailed rows are deleted, not just archived.
Account and configuration data is kept for as long as your account is active.
Delete your account and we cancel your subscriptions, stop your bot instances, and destroy your bot token immediately. The rest of your personal data is deleted within 30 days.
Stripe keeps payment records for as long as it’s legally required to, independent of what we do on our side.

whoWeShareWith.heading: Who we share it with
body: Stripe — payment processing and billing.
Google — sign-in, if you choose that method.
Resend — delivering account emails (sign-in links, alerts, receipts).
PostHog — product analytics, with session recording turned off.
Sentry — crash and error reporting, with tokens, passwords, and cookies stripped out before anything is sent.
Our hosting and infrastructure providers, to the extent needed to run the service.
We don’t sell personal data to anyone, and we never share your bot token in unencrypted form — not even with these providers.

cookiesAndAnalytics.heading: Cookies & analytics
body: We set one cookie to keep you signed in. It’s HttpOnly (scripts can’t read it), marked Secure, and expires after 30 days of inactivity.
We use PostHog to understand which features get used, with session recording disabled. We don’t run ad-tracking or cross-site cookies, and we don’t sell usage data to advertisers.

yourRights.heading: Your rights
body: Access or export the personal data we hold about you.
Correct inaccurate account details.
Delete your account and data — self-serve from Account settings, or by emailing us.
Object to non-essential email — though today, we only send you email your account actually needs (sign-in, billing, status alerts).
If you’re in Brazil, these rights are protected under the LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados). We apply the same rights to everyone who asks, regardless of where you live.

ageRequirement.heading: Age requirement
body: BotMaker is for adults: you must be 18 or older, or the age of majority where you live, and you confirm this when you sign up.
If we learn an account belongs to someone under that age, we refund the current billing period and suspend the account.

security.heading: Security
body: Your bot token is encrypted the moment it reaches us and is never returned by any part of the dashboard or API — only a last-4 reference is ever shown.

Traffic to and from BotMaker is encrypted in transit (TLS). Access to production systems is limited to what each part of our service actually needs — for example, the servers that run your bot don’t have access to billing data.
No system is perfectly secure, and we can’t promise otherwise — but token handling is the one thing we’ve deliberately over-engineered, because it’s the one thing that matters most here.

internationalTransfer.heading: International data transfers
body: Our company is Brazil-based, and some of the providers listed above (like Stripe, Google, PostHog, and Sentry) process data outside Brazil, including in the United States. Where that happens, we rely on those providers’ own safeguards for cross-border transfer.
By using BotMaker, you understand your data may be processed outside the country you live in.

changes.heading: Changes to this policy
body: If we make a material change to how we handle your data, we’ll update the date at the top of this page and, for significant changes, email you before they take effect.

contact.heading: Contact
body: Questions about this policy, or want to exercise one of the rights above? Email botmarket@codeswift.com.br.

terms.title: Terms of Service
intro: These terms cover your use of BotMaker — the dashboard, hosting, and catalog bots we operate. By creating an account or subscribing, you agree to them.
We’ve written these in plain language where we could. If something here conflicts with a specific consumer-protection law in your country, that law wins.

acceptance.heading: Acceptance of these terms
body: By creating a BotMaker account, you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy. You must be 18 or older, or the age of majority where you live, and you confirm this at signup.

whatWeProvide.heading: What we provide
body: BotMaker is a subscription service: you pick a bot from our first-party catalog, connect it to your own Highrise bot account using your own access token (“bring your own token,” or BYOT), configure it from a dashboard, and we host it for you around the clock.
We provide software and hosting. We do not sell, lease, or grant access to any Highrise account, bot, or in-game item — you already own the bot account before you connect it to us.

independentOperator.heading: Independent operator
body: BotMaker is an independent, unofficial project, operated by CodeSwift (codeswift.com.br). We are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Highrise or Pocket Worlds, and nothing in this product should be read as an official Highrise offering.
Your Highrise bot account remains subject to Highrise’s own Terms of Service at all times — ours don’t replace or override theirs.

eligibilityAndAccounts.heading: Eligibility & your account
body: You must be 18 or older, or the age of majority where you live, to create an account or subscribe.
You’re responsible for the accuracy of your account details and for keeping your sign-in secure. One account per person; accounts aren’t transferable.
If we learn an account belongs to someone under the required age, we refund the current billing period and suspend the account.

yourBotAndToken.heading: Your bot and your token
body: You own and are responsible for your Highrise bot account, including its compliance with Highrise’s Terms of Service and community rules in whatever room you run it in.
By pasting your bot’s access token into our dashboard, you authorize us to connect to Highrise as that bot and act on your instructions and configuration — nothing more.

You can revoke our access at any time by deleting your instance (which destroys our copy of the token immediately) or by regenerating the token in your Highrise account settings, which invalidates anything we ever held.

noGold.heading: No Highrise Gold, ever
body: We never accept, hold, request, or transfer Highrise Gold or any other in-game currency or item, for any reason. Every fee you pay us is billed in real currency only.
Our catalog bots are built the same way: none of them buy, sell, tip, or trade Gold or in-game items on your behalf.

acceptableUse.heading: Acceptable use
body: Don’t use BotMaker for anything illegal, or to harass, spam, or abuse other Highrise users.
Don’t configure a bot in a way designed to evade Highrise’s own moderation, rate limits, or account eligibility rules.
Don’t try to reverse-engineer, resell, or run unauthorized code through our service — our catalog bots are first-party only; you configure them, you don’t upload code to them.
Don’t attempt to disrupt, overload, or gain unauthorized access to our systems or another customer’s instance.
We may suspend or terminate an instance used for harassment, spam, or platform abuse, with or without notice depending on severity.

subscriptionAndBilling.heading: Subscription & billing
body: Each bot instance is billed as a monthly or annual subscription, in Brazilian reais (BRL) with a USD reference price shown for convenience, through Stripe.
A subscription entitles your instance to run; it doesn’t start the bot by itself. You press Start on the dashboard whenever you want it live, and Stop whenever you don’t.
Cancel anytime from the dashboard’s billing portal — your instance keeps running through the end of the period you already paid for.

refunds.heading: Refunds
body: First purchase, any plan: full refund within 7 days, no questions asked. This also satisfies Brazil’s consumer-protection right of withdrawal for online purchases (CDC Art. 49).

After that window, cancelling stops future renewals, but we don’t pro-rate a refund for the time already paid — with one exception: if we discontinue BotMaker or a bot you’re subscribed to, we refund any unused prepaid time.

paymentIssuesAndSuspension.heading: Payment issues
body: If a renewal payment fails, your bot keeps running for a short grace period (currently 3 days) while we email you to update your payment method.
If payment still hasn’t gone through after that, we suspend the instance — the bot stops, but your configuration is kept. Paying brings it back; you’ll need to press Start again.
If an instance stays unpaid for an extended period (currently 30 days from cancellation or suspension), we may delete it. We’ll offer to export your configuration before that happens.

terminationForAbuse.heading: Suspension & termination for abuse
body: Separate from payment issues, we can suspend or terminate your access if you violate these terms, misuse the service, or if we’re required to by law — for example, an instance used for harassment or spam.
Where practical, we’ll tell you why. For serious abuse, we may act first and explain after.

serviceAvailability.heading: Service availability
body: We host your bot to run continuously and work to keep it that way, but we don’t guarantee a specific uptime percentage at this stage — this isn’t a formal SLA.
We’re not responsible for outages, rate limiting, or account actions on Highrise’s side — those are Highrise’s systems, not ours, and outside our control.

intellectualProperty.heading: Intellectual property
body: Our catalog bots, dashboard, and underlying software are our property (or licensed to us). Your subscription gives you the right to configure and use them — it doesn’t transfer ownership of any of it to you.
Anything you enter into your configuration (welcome messages, filter words, and similar) stays yours; you’re responsible for making sure it doesn’t violate these terms or Highrise’s rules.

disclaimersLiability.heading: Disclaimers & limitation of liability
body: BotMaker is provided “as is.” We work to keep bots online and well-behaved, but we can’t guarantee they’ll prevent every moderation issue, or that Highrise won’t change its platform, rate limits, or eligibility rules in ways that affect your bot.
To the extent permitted by law, our liability to you is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the issue arose, and we’re not liable for indirect or consequential damages.
Nothing here limits rights that Brazilian consumer law (or another law that applies to you) doesn’t allow us to limit.

governingLaw.heading: Governing law
body: These terms are governed by the laws of Brazil, where CodeSwift, the company behind BotMaker, is based. We’ll publish our registered legal name, CNPJ, and business address here once they’re finalized.
If you’re a consumer, this doesn’t take away any protection you’re entitled to under the mandatory law of the country you live in.

changes.heading: Changes to these terms
body: We may update these terms as the product changes. For material changes, we’ll update the date at the top of this page and email you before they take effect.

contact.heading: Contact
body: Questions about these terms? Email botmarket@codeswift.com.br.

support.title: Support
support.intro: Most questions about your bot, your subscription, or how BotMaker works are answered below. Can't find yours? Email us — we read every message ourselves.

contact.heading: Contact us
contact.body: Have a question about your bot, your subscription, or anything else? Send us an email and we'll get back to you.
contact.tip: If a bot's misbehaving, open its instance page, go to the Status log card, and hit “Copy diagnostics” first — paste that straight into your email, it's exactly what we'd ask for anyway.

faq.question: What is BotMaker, exactly?
faq.answer: BotMaker hosts a ready-made Highrise bot — Emcee — for your room. Emcee bundles emotes-on-command, greetings and VIP recognition, moderation, and outfit features into one bot. You configure it from a dashboard; we run it 24/7.

faq.question: Do I need my own Highrise bot account?
faq.answer: Yes. You create the bot account and generate its access token in Highrise — we never own or resell Highrise accounts. You paste the token into your dashboard once, and we take it from there.

faq.question: Does BotMaker ever touch Highrise Gold?
faq.answer: No. All pricing is in real currency (BRL, with a USD reference price) — we never accept, hold, or transfer Gold in any form.

faq.question: Is my bot token safe?
faq.answer: It's encrypted at rest, write-only from the dashboard — once saved, no screen or API ever displays or returns it — and it's never written to logs.

faq.question: How much does it cost, and can I cancel anytime?
faq.answer: One flat price per bot instance, billed monthly or annually — see Pricing above. Pay by card. Cancel anytime; your bot keeps running until the end of the period you already paid for.

faq.question: Can I get a refund?
faq.answer: Yes — your first purchase on any plan is fully refundable within 7 days, no questions asked. After that, cancelling stops future renewals, but we don't pro-rate the current period.

faq.question: My bot looks offline or isn't responding — what do I do?
faq.answer: Open the bot's instance page and check the Status log card — it shows the current connection state and recent events. If something looks wrong, hit “Copy diagnostics” and paste the result into an email to us.

faq.question: Can I upload my own bot code?
faq.answer: Not today. Catalog bots are first-party — you configure them through the dashboard rather than uploading or running your own code on our infrastructure.
